title: A copy keeps following the original on the sides of its room it did not touch
goal: A copy of a component can already be given more room on one side, and the other three are left alone. What it cannot do is keep FOLLOWING the original on those three: answering any one side quietly hands the copy all four, so when the component is made roomier later, every copy anybody ever nudged is skipped and nothing on screen says why. This makes each side of a copy's room follow the original, or be the copy's own, on its own.
notes: Rewritten 2026-09-08 after the original premise expired. The old notes said the padding slot returns nil when the sides disagree; that has not been true since 19b75988 (2026-09-06), which gave ComponentPropertyValue a .room(GroupPadding) case so the knob carries all four sides. Four separate side knobs are explicitly NOT wanted (Add menu bloat, 264pt panel). What is left is partial following: ComponentPropertyValue.room holds a whole GroupPadding, so setInstanceRoom reads the original's four sides, writes one and stores all four as the copy's answer. Doing this means the stored answer has to record WHICH sides were answered (an optional per side, or an answered-side set beside the room) and the resolve path in ComponentProperties has to merge answered sides over the original's rather than replacing. Panel work is in ComponentPanel.sides(of:): per-side ink and a per-side revert. Blocked on the decision room-on-one-side-can-be-a-knob-when-a-copy-of-a-component-is-gi. Was titled 'Room on one side can be a knob'.
acceptance: Typing one side of a copy's room leaves the other three following the original, so changing the original's padding still reaches them
A copy's panel shows which sides are the copy's own and which are still following, and each side the copy owns has its own way back
A group whose four sides agree still offers the single Padding knob it offers today, not four extra rows
Tests in PhotonzCore cover it before the app code is written

Adversarial review before building, and the premise did not survive it. The task says a card with 16 beside and 10 above 'cannot offer its room to copies at all today'. That stopped being true about an hour after this task was written: 'Room that differs side to side can be a knob too' landed the same day (19b75988, 2026-09-06) and the room knob now carries all four sides. So three of the four acceptance items are already met, and the shortest version of what is left is nothing at all until one question is answered.

Checked each acceptance item against the app as it stands rather than assuming. (1) Room on a group whose sides disagree IS offered, as one Padding knob rather than four rows. (2) A copy shows it as a number field per side, opened by a chevron, and typing one side leaves the other three alone at that moment. (3) A group whose four sides agree still gets exactly one Padding row, so the Add menu never grew. (4) 23 tests cover it in PhotonzCore. Evidence: Scripts/test.sh --filter 'ComponentRoomKnobTests|ComponentRoomOfferTests' passes 23 tests in 2 suites, including typingOneSideKeepsTheOtherThree and typingOneSideOverTwoCopiesKeepsEachOnesOwnThree.

Four knobs, one per side, was the shape this task proposed and it is the wrong shape. Its own notes say four extra rows per group is the bloat the kind-grouped Add menu exists to stop, and the copy's panel is 264pt wide. One room knob with four sides behind a chevron is the canvas control a person already knows, so it costs no new idea and no new rows. Not building four knobs.

One thing the task asks for is genuinely missing, and I reproduced it rather than reading it. Temporary test in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests (removed after): a copy types Left 40, then the author changes the ORIGINAL's top from 10 to 32. Printed: 'after typing left 40: top 10, right 16, bottom 10, left 40' then 'original top -> 32, copy now: top 10, right 16, bottom 10, left 40'. So answering one side quietly takes the whole knob over and freezes the other three at whatever the original happened to be. Acceptance item 2 says the other three should stay the original's; today they only stay the original's numbers, not the original's.

That is a UX bargain the user should pick, not a bug I should decide: the audit for the knob already raised it on 2026-09-06 (queue/audits/2026-09-06-uneven-room-knob.json, evaluate question 3 and the third rough line) and it was never answered. Decision opened; blocked on it. If the answer is that untouched sides keep following, this task comes back with real work in it. If the answer is that an answer takes the whole knob, the task retires, because everything else in it already shipped.

Retitled and rewritten so the dashboard stops showing a goal that is no longer true. The old goal said a card with uneven room 'cannot offer its room to copies at all today' (A card with 16 points of room at the sides and 10 at the top...), which the four-sided room knob fixed on 2026-09-06. Acceptance now names the one thing actually left: the sides a copy did not touch should keep following the original.

Three of the four acceptance items already shipped on 2026-09-06 with the four-sided room knob (19b75988), verified by running the 23 tests in ComponentRoomKnobTests and ComponentRoomOfferTests. The fourth is real and I reproduced it: a copy typed to left 40 keeps top 10 even after the original's top is changed to 32, because answering one side hands the copy all four. Whether the untouched sides should keep following is a UX bargain the user picks, and the knob's own audit asked it in September and was never answered, so it is a decision card now. Task retitled and its goal rewritten to the one thing left.
decision "When a copy of a component is given more room on one side, should the other three sides keep following the original?" resolved: Untouched sides keep following
claimed by go loop

Adversarial review before building, second pass (the first pass ended in the decision card, now answered 'Untouched sides keep following'). Walked it as a person: I open a copy's Padding chevron, type 56 into Left, and the other three boxes go on showing the original's numbers. Nothing on screen would tell me those three are still the original's rather than mine, and that is the whole difference the answer buys, so it has to be visible or the change is invisible. Two places it can be seen without new chrome: the four boxes in the popout (my own side in ordinary ink, the three still following one step quieter), and a way back per side, which is the same uturn arrow the knob's row already wears.

Built it. Core: ComponentPropertyValue.room now carries a ComponentRoomAnswer (four optionals) instead of a whole GroupPadding, so a side nobody typed in is ABSENT rather than frozen. instanceValue resolves the copy's own sides over the original's, GroupLayout.setKnobValue merges rather than replaces (the one place following actually happens, and it works for both a knob on a piece inside and one on the copy's own edges because the original's room is already in the layout by the time the answer is written), setInstanceRoom adds one side to the copy's own answer, and a new clearInstanceRoomSide takes one back. An answer that owns no side is stored as no answer at all, so the row's way back goes away with the last side. Every older shape still opens owning all four: one number from before room had sides, and four numbers from before sides could follow separately.

Panel: FourSidedPopout.Number gained isOwn and handBack, both defaulted so the canvas Padding and Corner Radius popouts are byte for byte the popouts they were. A side the copy owns reads in ordinary ink with an uturn arrow beside it (named 'Follow again Left' and so on for walks); a side still following reads at the Mixed strength, via a new isFollowing on PanelNumberField. The arrow column is reserved whenever the popout offers any way back, so the little cross does not jump sideways the moment somebody types in it. The knob's row tooltip names which sides are the copy's own and which still follow.

Verified: 18 new tests in ComponentRoomFollowingTests, and the whole suite green at 8053 tests in 642 suites. swift build clean. Acceptance 1, 3 and 4 are covered by tests (theSidesNobodyTypedGoOnFollowingTheOriginal, theCopysOwnEdgesFollowSideBySideToo, twoCopiesEachKeepFollowingWhereTheyDidNotType; the Add menu is untouched so a group whose sides agree still gets exactly one Padding row). Acceptance 2 is built but NOT seen: see the next line.
